_doc: pc/tools/ps1_source_edits.py: PS1-width members of records that live in PS1 memory (audit_ps1_pointer_casts.py RECORD-PTR), retyped to 4-byte cells for the PC build only (matched sources unedited).  edits: [old, new(, count)] exact replacements, line count kept.  A stale entry stops the build.

main/GsTMDdivF3L.why: GsOT is a PS1-layout record (ot_work, 20-byte stride in vblank_function; org at +4 as tmd_gte_builders.c reads it) and the divide work area (the scratchpad Work/GsWORK, shared with the retail divide routines) keeps its console layout: OT pointer at +20, slot pointers at +168/+240.  The pointer members become 4-byte cells; the OT bucket address is the console's 32-bit sum (element size written out); the slot pointers are stored as 32-bit handles.  Nothing in the file reads them back.

main/get_dstack.why: GsCOORD0 (the old GsCOORDINATE: super at +32, sub at +36) and the 40-byte matrix-stack records at GsDSTACK (coordinate at +4; GsGetObjLw walks them at a 40-byte stride) are PS1 memory: the links become 4-byte cells, read back zero-extended; the chain cursor `*pp` is the caller's 4-byte cell (GsGetObjLw passes &tmp, an s32), so it is read and written 4 bytes wide

main/get_dstack2.why: GsCOORD0 (the old GsCOORDINATE: super at +32, sub at +36) and the 40-byte matrix-stack records at GsDSTACK (coordinate at +4; GsGetObjLw walks them at a 40-byte stride) are PS1 memory: the links become 4-byte cells, read back zero-extended

main/GsInitCoordinate.why: GsCOORD0 (the old GsCOORDINATE: super at +32, sub at +36) and the 40-byte matrix-stack records at GsDSTACK (coordinate at +4; GsGetObjLw walks them at a 40-byte stride) are PS1 memory: the links become 4-byte cells, read back zero-extended

main/GsSetRefView.why: GsRVIEW2.super is a 32-bit GsCOORDINATE2 handle at +28 on the console (the pc-port GsSetRefView2 reads it the same way)

main/GsLinkObject.why: the 112-byte coordinate record keeps its console layout: p100 / p104 / link are 32-bit cells at +100 / +104 / +108

main/GsLinkObject2.why: the element pointer is a 32-bit cell at +8 of the console record

main/mul_dmat.why: the 40-byte matrix-stack record at GsDSTACK: coordinate at +4 (a 4-byte cell, get_dstack writes it), the cached matrix at +8

main/mul_dmat_light.why: the 40-byte matrix-stack record at GsDSTACK: coordinate at +4 (a 4-byte cell, get_dstack writes it)

main/mul_rdmat.why: the 40-byte matrix-stack record at GsDSTACK (GsSetRefView walks it at a 40-byte stride): coordinate at +4, a 4-byte cell get_dstack2 writes

main/bustup_sprite_init.why: arg2 is the bust-up image block whose first word is a 4-byte PS1 pointer cell (the frame table); `p = *arg2` read it 8 bytes wide (UBSan, scenes 80 / 91).  Read as a cell, zero-extended

main/msg_str_disp.why: The console's frame (0x80081398: addiu sp,-0x2f8; prefix at sp+0x84, buf at sp+0x8c, tmpBuf at sp+0x28c, work at sp+0x2a4) puts tmpBuf right after buf[512], so strcpy(buf, str) of a longer message runs on into tmpBuf, which every reader rewrites first (strcpy/sprintf): harmless there.  Rei's ending epilogue (ENDING ending_result_disp) passes a 530-byte message: on the port GCC's frame put the stack canary after buf and the run aborted (stack smashing, found by the checkpoint suite, end_12_rei).  The three buffers become one record in the console's order; prefix stays a local.

ENDING/ending_serifu_cmd.why: tbl (the caller's sss_so, a PS1 address) is a table of 4-byte PS1 row pointers, each a table of 4-byte entry pointers; declared `s32 ***tbl`, the PC build read tbl[row] and [col] 8 bytes wide (two console cells as one pointer) on the portrait arm (cases 1 / 12 / ..): the UBSan explorer run card-end_00_shiori-s3 reported a null s32 load at each `tbl[row][col][0]`.  The parameter is an s32 (the caller passes sss_so, an s32, through the generator's unprototyped view of this K&R definition) and each level is read as a 4-byte cell and zero-extended, as the console's lw does.

DATE2/date2_serifu_prefix_set.why: pp is a PS1 cell (ss_serifu's entry +4, a 4-byte pointer to the serifu's string pointer); `p = *pp` read the u8 * 8 bytes wide, so the console's next cell became the pointer's high half.  Read as a 4-byte cell and zero-extended (found reading the explorer's ENDING finding's siblings, 2026-11-01).

TACO/taco_fan_disp.why: `out` is the caller's `s32 buf[40]` (taco_burst_disp, 160 bytes at sp+64 of the console's 224-byte frame): forty 4-byte PS1 primitive handles.  Declared `Prim **out` and walked with q++, the PC build stored forty 8-byte pointers, 320 bytes, past the buffer: the stack protector aborted the port in TACO's game (explorer, card-ev_final_taco98-s2, sub-step 11).  Each cell is a 4-byte handle, zero-extended where it is used.

ETC/etc_menu_dispatch.why: general_path walks etc_bg_tbl, a PS1 table of 4-byte pointers to the value tables: `slot2 = (s32 **)&etc_bg_tbl + a2; table = *slot2;` strode and read 8 bytes on the host (cell a2 at +8*a2, two console cells as one pointer), and the compare chain `slot2 == (s32 **)&etc_bg_tbl_1 ..` tested host-stride addresses against the console's 4-byte cell addresses (only a2 = 0 matched one).  slot2 is a u32 cell pointer, the cell zero-extended where it is read (audit_ps1_pointer_cells.py PS1-CELL, 2026-11-01).

OPTION/option_menu1_main1.why: p walks option_menu1_lbl_tbl, a PS1 table of 4-byte string pointers (the debug menu's labels, `extern u8 *option_menu1_lbl_tbl[]`): `debug_string_show(*p, ..); p++;` read 8 bytes per label (two console cells as one pointer) and strode 8.  p is a u32 cell pointer, each label zero-extended where it is passed (audit_ps1_pointer_cells.py PS1-CELL, 2026-11-01).

main/ContDataEntry.why: SsUtGetProgAtr(ch, prog, &count) fills a program record: bytes 0..4 and the halfword at +6 (sb x5, sh at out+6).  On the console `count` is the byte at sp+188 of ContDataEntry's 216-byte frame (addiu a2,sp,188 at 0x80093AEC) and sp+189..195 are frame bytes nothing else in the function touches (its other slots: 64/68, 88..116, 136, 156..187, 216/220), so the record's other seven bytes land harmlessly.  On the port `u8 count` is one byte at a GCC-chosen (odd) address: the record ran seven bytes into the neighbouring locals, and the explorer's UBSan campaign reported the halfword store misaligned at every boot (SsUtGetProgAtr.c:39-44, `out` = &count, an address on the game stack, 2026-11-01; filed then as an odd `_svm_pg`).  count becomes the first byte of an 8-byte, 4-aligned record, as the console's frame gives it.
